{"sql":"SELECT COALESCE(g.GenreId, 0) AS GenreId, COALESCE(g.Name, 'Unknown') AS GenreName,
       ROUND(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 2) AS Revenue,
       SUM(il.Quantity) AS TotalQuantity,
       COUNT(DISTINCT t.TrackId) AS DistinctTracks
FROM InvoiceLine il
JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
LEFT JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
ORDER BY Revenue DESC;"}

I cannot compute profit margins by genre because the database does not contain any cost data (no cost per track, per album, or per invoice). To calculate profit margin you need revenue and cost so margin = (revenue - cost) / revenue; we only have revenue.

What the data does contain (helpful context): revenue by genre from sales (invoice lines). 24 genres have sales. Top 10 genres by revenue are:
- Rock: $826.65
- Latin: $382.14
- Metal: $261.36
- Alternative & Punk: $241.56
- TV Shows: $93.53
- Jazz: $79.20
- Blues: $60.39
- Drama: $57.71
- R&B/Soul: $40.59
- Classical: $40.59

If you want profit margins, we need one of these added to the database:
- a per-track or per-album cost column (preferred), or
- a per-genre cost allocation table, or
- a table of licensing/purchase costs per track or per sale.

I can then compute profit margin by genre once cost data is available. In the meantime I can provide additional revenue breakdowns (e.g., entire list of genres, quantities sold, or recent-period revenue) if helpful.
sql_used:
SELECT COALESCE(g.GenreId, 0) AS GenreId, COALESCE(g.Name, 'Unknown') AS GenreName,
       ROUND(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 2) AS Revenue,
       SUM(il.Quantity) AS TotalQuantity,
       COUNT(DISTINCT t.TrackId) AS DistinctTracks
FROM InvoiceLine il
JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
LEFT JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
ORDER BY Revenue DESC;
assumptions: "Profit margin" means gross profit margin = (revenue - cost) / revenue.
